newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says nine dead in army clashes with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Peru says nine dead in army clashes with rebels.

text.p: Three Peruvian soldiers and six guerrillas died in a string of clashes in recent weeks in the central provinces of Ayacucho and Junin, the army said on Friday.

Five Shining Path guerrilla camps were also destroyed, 11 rebels arrested, and a large quantity of arms and ammunition captured during sweeps by soldiers between Sept. 6 and Oct. 8, the Peruvian army added in a statement.

Although greatly weakened since the 1992 capture of its leader Abimael Guzman, the Maoist Shining Path Movement has maintained pockets of resistance in its homeland of Ayacucho, where it launched a war on the state in 1980, and the jungle regions of Junin.
Conflicts unleashed by the Shining Path and the smaller Tupac Amaru Rvolutionary Movement (MRTA) have caused about 30,000 deaths and $25 billion in infrastructure damage since 1980.
